issue_context.title: Home Connect: Washing machine no longer reports duration, finish time, program progress
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Since using core-2025.3.0b2 (and now b3), the finishing time, program progress and duration entities of my washing machine (Siemens WG44B2ABNL) are set to Unavailable, even though the washing machine is running and the operation state is correctly set to Running. It is reporting correctly that the door is closed and locked.

Remaining time and end time do appear correctly in the Home Connect app as per usual. 

Practically, I only use two kinds of programs on this washing machine, and the time reporting has never been a problem in Home Assistant thus far. 

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2025.3.0b3

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

core-2025.2.x

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

home_connect

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/home_connect/

### Diagnostics information

[config_entry-home_connect-d734ed987a1014808c5b4decec682508.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19044303/config_entry-home_connect-d734ed987a1014808c5b4decec682508.json)

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml

```

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt

```

### Additional information

Curiously, I also have a Siemens dishwasher, and it still properly shows the time entities that are missing for the washing machine.

I believe there are some big backend changes for this integration in 2025.3, so perhaps this is a minor issue that still needs some attention.

About the duration entity, in never should have worked for you, as it is only available for ovens, but it was created for all the appliances.

About the other entities, we made a change where the entities will be not available while the program is not running/paused/finished. I'm not sure what it the issue with that, while your appliance program is on the mentioned states it should be set at least to the value `unknown`. And whenever we get the information required for the entity, we set it.

Maybe we should provide more info at diagnostics to help us to diagnose the problem...
By now, could you show us how does the history look for the entities different from duration? maybe we can get something from there

For some reason, the Program Finish Time just got populated (the washing machine is running right now). Why it does so towards the end of the program is a complete mystery to me. Here's a screenshot of the logbook from a week ago, where you can see that the finish time gets updated every minute (and fluctuates slightly): Let me know if I can offer you more useful feedback than screenshots.

> About the duration entity, in never should have worked for you, as it is only available for ovens, but it was created for all the appliances.

You're right, my bad. I don't have any history specifically for the duration entity of the washing machine.

Finish time is working again then? cool! That can mean that the appliance was not sending reports about the program status or Home Assistant was not able to receive it (maybe connection issues)
Program progress should work also, as they use exactly the same logic, if it isn't working maybe it is because the mentioned reasons.

> Finish time is working again then? cool! That can mean that the appliance was not sending reports about the program status or Home Assistant was not able to receive it (maybe connection issues) Not sure. Keep in mind that the Home Connect app, which I presume uses the same API, got the duration and end time during the entire washing cycle. This behavior of "reporting the finish time near the end" happened earlier today as well. Showing you a history graph with Operation State and Finish Time: As you can see, in the finish time row, a red/orange block appears towards the end of the running cycle, but there's no finish time before that. Going back to February 24, you can see that I had finish times during an entire washing cycle (actually two in short order):

> Home Connect app, which I presume uses the same API

Sorry, they don't use the same API. This is something we recently added to the documentation because people think (I did that too, before Home Connect support explained to me) that the integration and the app use the same API but doesn't.

I would suggest you to try running a program again to try confirm if it was something wrong with the Home Connect API or something else, because with my dishwasher I'm getting the finish time values:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4cd3ea59-133e-494f-8981-1c8e9a2ef81e)

> because with my dishwasher I'm getting the finish time values: Same here, with my Siemens dishwasher: The problem seems to be specific to the washing machine, not the dishwasher (as in your case). I'm sure I'll do more laundry in the next few days to see if this issue persists. Another thing I could try, though it might be somewhat disruptive and costs more time, is to revert to 2025.2 and see if the issue magically disappears.
Biting the bullet and restoring a backup of 2025.2. Will do laundry straight after.

After restoring a backup of **2025.2**, I started a new washing cycle (same settings as this afternoon), and as expected, the program finish time entity is populated immediately (added some text in red to aid non-Dutch readers): For good measure, while the washing machine was still running, I restored the backup of **2025.3.0b3** to get back to the state I was in at the time of opening this issue. After HA was running again, I waited 10 minutes to give the Home Connect API time to send data to my instance (which it seemingly does every minute, so 10 minutes is plenty). As before with 2025.3.0b3, the program finish time is unavailable again: I hope this confirms sufficiently that this is not a networking issue or an issue with the Home Connect API, but rather a result of the big changes made to this integration for 2025.3.
Please capture debug logs from the integration and its library during a run.

Enabled debug logging while the washing machine is running. I'll keep it running until after the Program finish time goes from Unavailable to an actual time by the end of the cycle, assuming this will happen again.

I think we don't update the `available` property on the entity to `True` for some reason.

I think we need to change the logic for the `available` property to be more pragmatic. If updates are coming in for an entity we should always mark it as available, regardless of past state. Eg we may have missed a CONNECTED event or the last poll was unsuccessful. But if we after that receive a valid update to an entity it should be made available.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
   Unavailable: Unavailable
    note right of Unavailable
        We set it to unavailable because there are some events from Home Connect that sends wrong values
    end note
    Value: Value from the event
    [*] --> Unavailable
    Unavailable --> Unknown: program status is running and program remaining time or progress event has not been received yet
    Unavailable --> Value:  program remaining time or progress event is received and then program status running is received
    Unknown --> Value: Event with new information is received by the entity
    Value --> Unavailable: Program is longer running/paused/finished. value is set to None delete the last value
```

Code for reference:
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/7e4432e321cedeedbfe4d7a45eb40b7078e5f5e9/homeassistant/components/home_connect/sensor.py#L350-L391

I think I have faced the same issue
Do you know, @richardvinger, if the appliance was already running a program while the integration was starting?
Because something that I realized, is that we don't check the status of the operation state at the start, we only check it when we update it

@Diegorro98 I've had both, i.e. when I downgraded to 2025.2, I had Home Assistant and the integration running _before_  the appliance was running a program. Then, when upgrading to a beta version of 2025.3, the wash program was still running while the integration was loading

It looks like now there's a regression in 2025.3.2? I'm seeing strange behavior again. The issue now is that the integration says my washing machine is "ready" and the door is "open", while in reality, it is running a program now. 

Another issue I'm observing with the dish washer is that both the dish washer itself and the Home Connect app say that salt is low, though that isn't reflected in HA ("Salt nearly empty" is off). Let me know if you prefer me to open a separate issue for this.

Attaching a diagnostics log.

Please open a separate issue for each problem.

review_comments:
I understand that we do this because we set all the appliances' connected attribute to `False` here:
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/f2fd334615ee0d2a156098e0219228910c23a340/homeassistant/components/home_connect/coordinator.py#L265-L276
Right?
What if an appliance doesn't not send any event when stream is opened? If `EventStreamInterruptedError`, `HomeConnectRequestError` are raised, the appliance will not be shown as connected until an event from that appliance is received.

This is the case of my dishwasher; While it isn't running any program or no one does nothing on the dishwasher (physically, through the app or through the API), it doesn't send any event, it can stay without sending any event forever.

A successful coordinator refresh will make the appliance connected and entities available. So after that there's doesn't need to be an event to make the appliance connected and entities available. But if the appliance went to a non connected state for some reason, I think it's reasonable to require at least one event or successful refresh before marking it as connected again.

What do you think?
What we should do, I think, is to forward the keep alive events too.

We can remove the change of connected state when the event stream is interrupted non breaking, and discuss that more. It's not required to fix the reported bug. The required change is here on line 169.

Do we perform a coordinator refresh after `EventStreamInterruptedError`, `HomeConnectRequestError`?
Before #139740 I know we did it, but right now we aren't AFAIK.

About forward the keep alive events, because KEEP-ALIVE events' haId is always the same than the last one sent or empty string, they can fix the issue for a particular case, but also raise another issues.
- For an user that only has one appliance, it will set the appliance as connected as soon as a KEEP-ALIVE event is received
- If an DISCONNECTED event is received from an appliance, the next KEEP-ALIVE event will set the appliance as connected if there isn't any event from other appliance before

Right.

There's no refresh now after interrupted event stream.

Should we remove the change of connected state on interrupted event stream then?

Maybe. I mean, if we remove the change, the worst that can happen is that appliances that have been connected or disconnected doesn't update their state because the stream is down, but we can solve that when we reimplement the refresh, right?
Ok, I removed it for now.
